units.text: The allergen rules for every product sold at Crumbwick Bakery.
units.label: description

units.text: Allergens
units.label: none

units.text: Nuts, milk, egg, sesame and gluten are the five allergens that appear in our products.
units.label: description

units.text: Gluten appears in every loaf, so the gluten line is printed on every label.
units.label: description

units.text: Labels
units.label: none

units.text: Print the allergen label for every new product before it goes on a shelf.
units.label: gate

units.text: Read the recipe card to the head baker before you print a new label.
units.label: gate

units.text: Never guess an allergen from the name of a product.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: For example, a poppy roll can still carry sesame if it shares a tray with sesame buns.
units.label: example

units.text: Put the label on the front of the sack, not on the back.
units.label: rule

units.text: Answering customers
units.label: none

units.text: Say plainly which allergens a product contains
units.label: rule

units.text: Offer the allergen folder if the customer asks for more detail
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not say that anything is free of nuts
units.label: prohibition

units.text: The allergen folder sits on the counter by the till
units.label: description

units.text: Cross contact
units.label: none

units.text: The walnut loaf is baked on its own tray in the small oven.
units.label: description

units.text: Wash the walnut tray in its own sink with its own cloth.
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not bake a walnut loaf and a sesame bun in the same oven load.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Wipe the small oven deck clean before the walnut loaf goes in.
units.label: gate

units.text: Case: a nut free customer reacted to a bun that was baked after the walnut loaf on a dirty deck.
units.label: example

units.text: Emergencies
units.label: none

units.text: Call the emergency number first if a customer reacts to food.
units.label: gate

units.text: Tell the shop manager after the call.
units.label: gate

units.text: The emergency number is written on the wall beside the sconce room door.
units.label: description

units.text: Stay calm and speak clearly.
units.label: rule

units.text: The cleaning schedule for the shop, the loft and the back rooms of Crumbwick Bakery.
units.label: description

units.text: Cleaning
units.label: none

units.text: The shop is cleaned every day and the loft and back rooms are cleaned every week.
units.label: description

units.text: The cleaning cupboard is the tall green cupboard in the back corridor.
units.label: description

units.text: Daily
units.label: none

units.text: Sweep the shop floor from the walls toward the door
units.label: rule

units.text: Mop the floor with the blue bucket
units.label: rule

units.text: Empty the crumb tray under each shelf
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not use the blue bucket in the loft
units.label: prohibition

units.text: The blue bucket is marked with a blue strip of tape
units.label: description

units.text: Surfaces
units.label: none

units.text: Wipe the counter and the till with the yellow cloth.
units.label: rule

units.text: Wipe the counter before you wipe the till.
units.label: gate

units.text: Never use the yellow cloth on the floor.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: For example, a yellow cloth used on the floor was found on the counter the next morning, grey with grit.
units.label: example

units.text: Weekly
units.label: none

units.text: Day
units.label: none

units.text: Area
units.label: none

units.text: Who
units.label: none

units.text: Monday
units.label: description

units.text: The loft
units.label: description

units.text: Opening crew
units.label: description

units.text: Wednesday
units.label: description

units.text: The cold room
units.label: description

units.text: Closing crew
units.label: description

units.text: Friday
units.label: description

units.text: The back corridor
units.label: description

units.text: Head baker
units.label: description

units.text: Clear the cold room shelves completely before you wash them on Wednesday.
units.label: gate

units.text: Do not wash the cold room shelves with hot water.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Unplug the cold room fan before you wipe its cover.
units.label: gate

units.text: Waste
units.label: none

units.text: Tie the waste bags with a double knot.
units.label: rule

units.text: Put the bags in the grey bins by the back door.
units.label: rule

units.text: Never put broken glass in a waste bag.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Broken glass goes in the red tin beside the cleaning cupboard.
units.label: description

units.text: Case: a bag with broken glass cut the hand of a collector last year.
units.label: example

units.text: Cleaning is everyone's job.
units.label: none

units.text: The closing routine of Crumbwick Bakery, from the last sale to the locked door.
units.label: description

units.text: Closing the shop
units.label: none

units.text: Closing takes about forty minutes and starts when the last customer has left.
units.label: description

units.text: Turn the street door sign to closed as soon as the last customer leaves.
units.label: rule

units.text: The ovens and lamps
units.label: none

units.text: Switch off both ovens before you switch off the lamps.
units.label: gate
units.section: Closing the shop > The ovens and lamps

units.text: Never leave an oven on overnight, even at the lowest setting.
units.label: prohibition
units.section: Closing the shop > The ovens and lamps

units.text: Pull the oven racks out and stand them upright on the cooling plinth.
units.label: rule
units.section: Closing the shop > The ovens and lamps

units.text: The cooling plinth is the long steel bench under the east window.
units.label: description
units.section: Closing the shop > The ovens and lamps

units.text: Switch off the front lamps only after the oven check is written in the closing book.
units.label: gate
units.section: Closing the shop > The ovens and lamps

units.text: For instance, a warm oven at closing means the check goes in the book with a note.
units.label: example
units.section: Closing the shop > The ovens and lamps

units.text: The shelves
units.label: none

units.text: Move unsold loaves into the paper sacks on the left shelf
units.label: rule

units.text: Label each sack with the day and the kind of loaf
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not put cream cakes in the sacks, because they spoil by morning
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Unsold sacks go to the food bank on Tuesday and Friday
units.label: description

units.text: A sack of six rye loaves marked Thursday goes out on Friday
units.label: example

units.text: The tills
units.label: none

units.text: Count the till drawer twice before you lock it in the sconce room.
units.label: gate

units.text: Write the total in the closing book and sign it.
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not carry the cash bag out of the shop at night.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: The closing book lives on the hook beside the sconce room door.
units.label: description

units.text: The door
units.label: none

units.text: Return every key to the sconce room before you lock the street door.
units.label: gate

units.text: Lock the street door with two turns of the brass key.
units.label: rule

units.text: The alarm panel gives you ninety seconds to leave once it is set.
units.label: description

units.text: Thank you for closing carefully.
units.label: none

units.text: How flour, butter and sacks are received at the back door of Crumbwick Bakery.
units.label: description

units.text: Deliveries
units.label: none

units.text: Deliveries arrive between six and eight on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday.
units.label: description

units.text: The flour driver is called Odalys and the butter driver is called Fenn.
units.label: description

units.text: Receiving
units.label: none

units.text: Count the sacks at the back door before you sign the driver's sheet.
units.label: gate

units.text: Check the date on each butter block.
units.label: rule

units.text: Sign the driver's sheet only after the count matches the sheet.
units.label: gate

units.text: Never let a driver leave sacks outside the back door.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: For example, a sack of tarn flour left in the rain on a Saturday had to be thrown away.
units.label: example

units.text: Storing
units.label: none

units.text: Put new flour sacks behind the old ones in the flour store
units.label: rule

units.text: Stand butter blocks in the cold room on the middle shelf
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not stack flour sacks higher than four
units.label: prohibition

units.text: The flour store is the dry room next to the back door
units.label: description

units.text: A stack of five sacks on the left wall tipped over last winter and split three of them
units.label: example

units.text: Problems
units.label: none

units.text: Phone the supplier if a sack is torn or a butter block is soft.
units.label: rule

units.text: Take a photo of a damaged sack before you move it.
units.label: gate

units.text: Do not use flour from a torn sack in the dough.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: A torn sack may let in damp and insects.
units.label: description

units.text: Case: flour from a torn sack went into a batch on a Thursday and the whole batch was binned.
units.label: example

units.text: Paperwork
units.label: none

units.text: Hand the signed sheet to the shop manager by noon.
units.label: rule

units.text: The shop manager files each sheet in the grey box.
units.label: description

units.text: Greet the drivers with a smile.
units.label: rule

units.text: The dough loft routine at Crumbwick Bakery, covering mixing, proving and shaping pinnocks.
units.label: description

units.text: The dough loft
units.label: none

units.text: A pinnock is the small round dough ball that every loaf at Crumbwick starts from.
units.label: description

units.text: The loft has a proving drawer, a mixing trough and a brass scale.
units.label: description

units.text: Mixing
units.label: none

units.text: Mix the tarn flour with cold water and let it rest for twenty minutes.
units.label: rule

units.text: Add the salt only after the flour has rested.
units.label: gate

units.text: Never use hot water in the trough, because it kills the starter.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: For example, a trough mixed with hot water on a summer day produced flat loaves for a whole week.
units.label: example

units.text: The starter is called Wobbin and it lives in the green crock on the top shelf.
units.label: description

units.text: Feed Wobbin with a spoon of flour and a spoon of water every evening.
units.label: rule

units.text: Proving
units.label: none

units.text: Place the shaped pinnocks on the linen in the proving drawer
units.label: rule

units.text: Close the proving drawer before you start the heater
units.label: gate

units.text: Do not open the proving drawer more than once an hour
units.label: prohibition

units.text: The proving drawer holds a steady warmth of twenty six degrees
units.label: description

units.text: A pinnock that has doubled in size after ninety minutes is ready for the oven
units.label: example

units.text: Shaping
units.label: none

units.text: Shape each pinnock with two hands and a light dusting of flour.
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not press the dough flat, because the crumb will turn dense.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Weigh each pinnock again after shaping and put any that are light back on the scale.
units.label: gate

units.text: A standard pinnock weighs four hundred and fifty grams.
units.label: description

units.text: Case: a light pinnock of four hundred grams baked into a loaf that the shop could not sell as standard.
units.label: example

units.text: Cleaning the loft
units.label: none

units.text: Scrape the trough with the plastic scraper and rinse it with cold water.
units.label: rule
units.section: The dough loft > Cleaning the loft

units.text: Do not wash the linen with soap, because the smell passes into the crumb.
units.label: prohibition
units.section: The dough loft > Cleaning the loft

units.text: Ask Marek if the starter smells odd.
units.label: rule
units.section: The dough loft > Cleaning the loft

units.text: The words used by the Crumbwick Bakery crew and what each one means.
units.label: description

units.text: Glossary
units.label: none

units.text: New crew members hear these words on their first morning.
units.label: description

units.text: Word
units.label: none

units.text: Meaning
units.label: none

units.text: Pinnock
units.label: description

units.text: A small round dough ball that is the start of a loaf
units.label: description

units.text: Sconce room
units.label: description

units.text: The small cupboard behind the till that holds the keys
units.label: description

units.text: Plinth
units.label: description

units.text: The steel bench under the east window where racks cool
units.label: description

units.text: Wobbin
units.label: description

units.text: The name of the sourdough starter
units.label: description

units.text: Tarn flour
units.label: description

units.text: The coarse flour from the hill mill
units.label: description

units.text: Usage
units.label: none

units.text: Use the word pinnock for the dough ball and never for a finished loaf.
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not call the sconce room the safe, because it holds keys and not money.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: For example, write that the opening crew carried six pinnocks down, not six loaves.
units.label: example

units.text: The word plinth comes from the old stone bench that once stood there.
units.label: description

units.text: Ask if you hear a word that is not here.
units.label: rule

units.text: Short forms
units.label: none

units.text: OB means the order book
units.label: description

units.text: CB means the closing book
units.label: description

units.text: SB means the shift book
units.label: description

units.text: Spell out a short form the first time you use it in a note
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not use a short form on a customer label
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Naming loaves
units.label: none

units.text: Give a new loaf a name of one or two words, and tell the head baker before you use it.
units.label: gate

units.text: Check the name against the allergen folder before it goes on a tag.
units.label: gate

units.text: The best known loaf is the Tarn Rye, which sells out by ten.
units.label: description

units.text: Case: a loaf called Nut Free Rye was named by a new crew member and had to be renamed the same day.
units.label: example

units.text: How the crew of Crumbwick Bakery opens the shop before the first customer arrives.
units.label: description

units.text: Opening the shop
units.label: none

units.text: The opening crew arrives at half past five and works until the doors open at seven.
units.label: description

units.text: Every morning follows the same order, and the order matters more than the speed.
units.label: description

units.text: Lamps and doors
units.label: none

units.text: Switch on the front lamps before you unlock the street door.
units.label: gate
units.section: Opening the shop > Lamps and doors

units.text: Unlock the street door with the brass key that hangs in the sconce room.
units.label: rule
units.section: Opening the shop > Lamps and doors

units.text: Never prop the back door open with a crate while the ovens are warm.
units.label: prohibition
units.section: Opening the shop > Lamps and doors

units.text: The sconce room is the small cupboard behind the till, and it holds every key.
units.label: description
units.section: Opening the shop > Lamps and doors

units.text: Check that the alarm panel shows a green light, then write the time in the opening book.
units.label: gate
units.section: Opening the shop > Lamps and doors

units.text: For example, if the panel shows an amber light, the night crew left a window open.
units.label: example
units.section: Opening the shop > Lamps and doors

units.text: Ovens
units.label: none

units.text: Light the big oven first and the small oven ten minutes later.
units.label: gate

units.text: Wait until the big oven reads two hundred and twenty degrees before the first tray goes in.
units.label: gate

units.text: The big oven holds twelve trays and the small oven holds four.
units.label: description

units.text: Do not load a cold tray into a hot oven, because the glaze will crack.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Case: a tray of pinnocks went in cold on a Monday and came out with split tops.
units.label: example

units.text: The dough loft
units.label: none

units.text: Carry the proved dough down from the dough loft in the wheeled bin
units.label: rule
units.section: Opening the shop > The dough loft

units.text: Weigh each pinnock on the brass scale before it is shaped
units.label: gate
units.section: Opening the shop > The dough loft

units.text: Do not stack more than three bins on the lift
units.label: prohibition
units.section: Opening the shop > The dough loft

units.text: The loft is warmest near the east window
units.label: description
units.section: Opening the shop > The dough loft

units.text: Final checks
units.label: none

units.text: Count the float in the till before you open the street door.
units.label: gate

units.text: Fill the front shelves from left to right, oldest loaves first.
units.label: rule

units.text: Customers usually form a line by ten past seven.
units.label: description

units.text: Thank you for opening well.
units.label: none

units.text: Good luck today.
units.label: none

units.text: How phone orders and party orders are taken and recorded at Crumbwick Bakery.
units.label: description

units.text: Taking orders
units.label: none

units.text: Orders come in by phone, by the paper form or at the counter.
units.label: description

units.text: Every order goes into the order book with a number.
units.label: description

units.text: Phone orders
units.label: none

units.text: Ask the caller for a name and a phone number before you take any details.
units.label: gate

units.text: Repeat the order back to the caller in full.
units.label: rule

units.text: Take a deposit before you write a party order in the book.
units.label: gate

units.text: Never promise a decorated cake with less than two days of notice.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: A party order is any order of more than twenty loaves or rolls.
units.label: description

units.text: For example, forty rolls for a school visit counts as a party order.
units.label: example

units.text: The order book
units.label: none

units.text: Write the pickup date at the top of the page
units.label: rule

units.text: Give each order the next number in the book
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not use pencil in the order book
units.label: prohibition

units.text: The order book is kept on the shelf under the till
units.label: description

units.text: Changes
units.label: none

units.text: Cross out a cancelled order with one straight line and write the reason beside it.
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not tear a page out of the order book.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Phone the customer before you change the size of a party order.
units.label: gate

units.text: Case: a party order of thirty loaves was cut to twenty without a call, and the customer arrived to a short count.
units.label: example

units.text: Pickup
units.label: none

units.text: Check the order number against the sack before you hand it over.
units.label: gate

units.text: Ask the customer to sign the book for any party order.
units.label: rule

units.text: Unclaimed orders are kept until the next morning and then go to the food bank.
units.label: description

units.text: The pickup shelf is the narrow shelf beside the street door.
units.label: description

units.text: Be kind to customers who are in a hurry.
units.label: rule

units.text: How to run, clean and report faults on the two ovens at Crumbwick Bakery.
units.label: description

units.text: Ovens
units.label: none

units.text: The big oven is a deck oven with three decks, and the small oven is a single deck.
units.label: description

units.text: Both ovens run on gas, and the gas tap sits behind the flour store.
units.label: description

units.text: Lighting
units.label: none

units.text: Open the gas tap before you press the spark button.
units.label: gate

units.text: Never press the spark button more than three times in a row.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: If the flame does not catch after three tries, close the tap and wait five minutes.
units.label: rule

units.text: Example: on a windy morning the pilot flame often blows out twice before it holds.
units.label: example

units.text: Call the gas engineer if the flame turns yellow instead of blue.
units.label: rule

units.text: Daily care
units.label: none

units.text: Brush the oven floor with the long brass brush after the last tray
units.label: gate

units.text: Wipe the oven door glass with the dry grey cloth
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not spray water on a hot deck
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Do not use the steel scraper on the door glass
units.label: prohibition

units.text: The grey cloth hangs on the hook beside the big oven
units.label: description

units.text: Weekly care
units.label: none

units.text: Soak the racks in the sink with warm water and the green soap every Sunday.
units.label: rule

units.text: Let the ovens cool completely before you soak the racks.
units.label: gate

units.text: A full soak takes about an hour and needs two people.
units.label: description

units.text: Case: one crew soaked a hot rack and the steel warped so badly that it had to be replaced.
units.label: example

units.text: Faults
units.label: none

units.text: Sign
units.label: none

units.text: What it means
units.label: none

units.text: What to do
units.label: none

units.text: Yellow flame
units.label: description

units.text: The gas mix is wrong
units.label: description

units.text: Close the tap and call the engineer
units.label: rule

units.text: Clicking with no flame
units.label: description

units.text: The spark button is damp
units.label: description

units.text: Dry the button with the grey cloth
units.label: rule

units.text: Smell of gas
units.label: description

units.text: A leak somewhere in the line
units.label: description

units.text: Open the doors and leave the shop
units.label: rule

units.text: Never switch on a lamp or the till if you smell gas.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Ask the opening crew if a fault looks new.
units.label: rule

units.text: The seasonal baking plan and special loaves of Crumbwick Bakery.
units.label: description

units.text: Seasonal baking
units.label: none

units.text: Crumbwick bakes four seasonal loaves each year: spring dill, summer fig, autumn oat and winter spice.
units.label: description

units.text: Seasonal loaves go on level two beside the pinnock loaves.
units.label: description

units.text: Winter spice loaf
units.label: none

units.text: Bake the winter spice loaf in the big oven only.
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not add the spice mix until the dough has risen once.
units.label: gate

units.text: Let the dough rise once before you add the spice mix.
units.label: gate

units.text: For example, a spice mix added at the start made the dough sticky and the crumb grey.
units.label: example

units.text: The spice mix has cinnamon, clove and a pinch of orrel seed.
units.label: description

units.text: Summer fig loaf
units.label: none

units.text: Soak the figs in warm water for ten minutes
units.label: rule

units.text: Dry the figs on a clean cloth
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not add wet figs to the dough
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Figs come in a box of sixty and arrive on Thursday
units.label: description

units.text: A fig loaf with wet figs split along the top in the oven
units.label: example

units.text: Orders for the season
units.label: none

units.text: Take Christmas orders from the first of November.
units.label: rule
units.section: Seasonal baking > Orders for the season

units.text: Check the oven plan for the week before you accept a big Christmas order.
units.label: gate
units.section: Seasonal baking > Orders for the season

units.text: Never accept a Christmas order after the twentieth of December.
units.label: prohibition
units.section: Seasonal baking > Orders for the season

units.text: The oven plan hangs on the wall of the dough loft.
units.label: description
units.section: Seasonal baking > Orders for the season

units.text: Case: a late order for sixty winter spice loaves took the whole oven for a night and the daily bread came late.
units.label: example
units.section: Seasonal baking > Orders for the season

units.text: Decorations
units.label: none

units.text: Hang the paper stars in the window on the first of December.
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not tape anything to the glass of the oven door.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: The shop looks lovely in the snow.
units.label: none

units.text: How loaves, rolls and cakes are placed on the front shelves of Crumbwick Bakery.
units.label: description

units.text: Shelf display
units.label: none

units.text: The front shelves have five levels and each level has a colour tag.
units.label: description

units.text: Customers read the shelves from the top down, so the best sellers go at eye height.
units.label: description

units.text: Levels
units.label: none

units.text: Level
units.label: none

units.text: Tag colour
units.label: none

units.text: Goes here
units.label: none

units.text: One
units.label: description

units.text: Red
units.label: description

units.text: Rye loaves and heavy loaves
units.label: description

units.text: Two
units.label: description

units.text: Blue
units.label: description

units.text: Pinnock loaves
units.label: description

units.text: Three
units.label: description

units.text: Green
units.label: description

units.label: description

units.text: Four
units.label: description

units.text: Rules of the shelf
units.label: none

units.text: Put the oldest loaves at the front of each level.
units.label: rule
units.section: Shelf display > Rules of the shelf

units.text: Wipe each level with a damp cloth before you refill it.
units.label: gate
units.section: Shelf display > Rules of the shelf

units.text: Never place cream cakes on level one, because the rye loaves press into them.
units.label: prohibition
units.section: Shelf display > Rules of the shelf

units.text: Do not cover the price tags with paper sacks.
units.label: prohibition
units.section: Shelf display > Rules of the shelf

units.text: Check the price tag before you put any new kind of loaf on a level.
units.label: gate
units.section: Shelf display > Rules of the shelf

units.text: For example, a new walnut loaf needs a fresh tag in the pinnock colour before it goes on level two.
units.label: example
units.section: Shelf display > Rules of the shelf

units.text: Gaps
units.label: none

units.text: Fill any gap on levels one to three within ten minutes
units.label: rule

units.text: Move a loaf forward when the one behind it sells
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not leave a half empty level at the lunch rush
units.label: prohibition

units.text: The lunch rush runs from noon to half past one
units.label: description

units.text: Sales signs
units.label: none

units.text: Place the chalk board by the door each morning and write the loaf of the day.
units.label: rule

units.text: Wipe the old chalk board clean before you write on it.
units.label: gate

units.text: The loaf of the day is chosen by the head baker.
units.label: description

units.text: Phone the shop manager at least one hour before the shift if you will be late.
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not swap a shift without the shop manager's written note.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Write the swap in the shift book before you tell the other person.
units.label: gate

units.text: Breaks
units.label: none

units.text: Take your break away from the ovens and the loft
units.label: rule

units.text: Wash your hands before you return to the shelves
units.label: gate

units.text: Do not eat on the shop floor
units.label: prohibition

units.text: The break room is the small room at the end of the back corridor
units.label: description

units.text: A crew member who ate a roll behind the till left crumbs that a customer later complained about
units.label: example

units.text: Uniform
units.label: none

units.text: Wear the white apron and the grey cap in the loft and at the ovens.
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not wear rings in the loft.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Aprons are washed on Sunday by the closing crew.
units.label: description

units.text: Case: a ring dropped into a trough once and the whole batch of dough had to be searched.
units.label: example

units.text: Asking for help
units.label: none

units.text: Ask the head baker if you do not know a step.
units.label: rule

units.text: Write a question in the question book if the head baker is away.
units.label: rule

units.text: Read the question book at the start of each shift.
units.label: gate

units.text: The question book lies on the table in the break room.
units.label: description

units.text: Nobody minds a good question.
units.label: none

units.text: How the two tills at Crumbwick Bakery are opened, used and counted.
units.label: description

units.text: Tills
units.label: none

units.text: There are two tills, one at the street door and one at the pickup shelf.
units.label: description

units.text: Each till has its own drawer key, and the keys live in the sconce room.
units.label: description

units.text: Opening a till
units.label: none

units.text: Count the float in the drawer before you log in.
units.label: gate

units.text: Log in with your own crew number.
units.label: rule

units.text: Never share a crew number with another person.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: For example, a shared number made it impossible to find who had given a wrong change on a Saturday.
units.label: example

units.text: The float is eighty pounds in coins and notes.
units.label: description

units.text: Taking payment
units.label: none

units.text: Say the total aloud before the customer pays
units.label: gate

units.text: Offer a receipt with every sale
units.label: rule

units.text: Do not open the drawer without a sale
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Do not write a card number on paper
units.label: prohibition

units.text: The card reader sits on the left of each till
units.label: description

units.text: Mistakes
units.label: none

units.text: Call the shop manager to void a sale, and wait for the manager to key the void.
units.label: rule

units.text: Keep the receipt of the wrong sale before the manager voids it.
units.label: gate

units.text: Never void your own sale.
units.label: prohibition

units.text: Case: a crew member voided a sale of two loaves and kept the cash, and the count was short by that amount.
units.label: example

units.text: The shop manager holds the void key on a red cord.
units.label: description

units.text: Counting
units.label: none

units.text: Count the drawer twice at closing and write both counts in the book.
units.label: rule

units.text: Ask a second person to count it if the two counts differ.
units.label: gate

units.text: A difference of more than two pounds is reported to the shop manager.
units.label: description

units.text: Take your time with the count.
units.label: rule

blocks.name: closing-order
blocks.description: A closing crew member is told the evening is going well and asks to kill the shop lamps first to save time. The agent must have the crew switch off the ovens first and record the oven check before anything goes dark.

blocks.name: overnight-warmth
blocks.description: The crew wants the small oven kept at its lowest setting overnight so the first batch heats fast. The agent has to say no and tell them what to do with the oven at closing.

blocks.name: last-out
blocks.description: The last person leaving the shop has already pulled the street door shut and still holds the key ring and the till drawer. The agent must make them put the keys and the counted drawer back in the cupboard before locking up.

blocks.name: food-bank-sacks
blocks.description: Leftover goods are being packed for the food bank at the end of the day. A cream cake is offered for the sack. The agent must keep it out and make sure the sack is set up the usual way.

blocks.name: yellow-flame
blocks.description: A baker reports that the big oven burns with a yellow flame instead of blue. The agent must send the problem to the right outside person.

blocks.name: gas-smell
blocks.description: A crew member smells gas near the oven and reaches for the lamp switch and the till to see if the power is on. The agent must stop them.

blocks.name: hot-deck-spray
blocks.description: Someone wants to speed up cleaning by spraying water on the oven deck right after the last tray. The agent must refuse and say what to do instead.

blocks.name: dough-mix-order
blocks.description: A new baker asks when the salt goes into the trough and whether warm water from the tap is fine in summer. The agent must give the right order and refuse the hot water.

blocks.name: starter-evening
blocks.description: At the end of the day a baker asks whether the starter has to be fed or can be skipped for the weekend. The agent must give the usual care for it.

blocks.name: cream-cake-level
blocks.description: A crew member is rearranging the front display and wants to put the cream cakes on the lowest-numbered level next to the heavy loaves because there is space. The agent must stop it.

blocks.name: new-loaf-launch
blocks.description: The head baker wants to put a brand new loaf on the display this morning. The agent must walk the crew through the three things needed first: the tag, the printed allergen label with the recipe read out, and a name cleared with the head baker.

blocks.name: party-order-call
blocks.description: A school phones in an order for forty rolls and a decorated cake for the day after tomorrow. The agent must have the crew gather the caller's details, take money before booking, and decline the cake.

blocks.name: allergen-question
blocks.description: A customer asks if the poppy roll is nut free and says the label is hard to read. The agent must answer from the recipe card and refuse to promise anything is free of an allergen, and must not guess from the name.

blocks.name: walnut-bake
blocks.description: The crew has a walnut loaf and a tray of buns to bake in the small oven in one go. The agent must make them clean the deck first.

blocks.name: delivery-door
blocks.description: The flour driver is in a hurry, hands over a sheet and offers to dump the sacks on the step. The agent must make the crew check the numbers before signing and refuse the step.

blocks.name: torn-sack
blocks.description: A flour sack has a long tear and the baker says the flour is fine to use today. The agent must say no.

blocks.name: own-void
blocks.description: A crew member rang a wrong amount and wants to cancel the sale on the till without bothering anyone. The agent must route it to the right person and keep the crew member from doing it.

blocks.name: late-christmas
blocks.description: On the twenty second of December a regular asks for sixty winter spice loaves for Christmas Eve. The agent must refuse the order and say what would have been needed earlier in the process.

blocks.name: shift-swap
blocks.description: A crew member will be late on Friday and has also arranged with a colleague to swap their closing shift. The agent must say who to phone and in what order the swap is recorded.

blocks.name: broken-glass-bag
blocks.description: A jar shatters at the back and the cleaner wants to sweep the pieces into the nearest waste bag and carry it to the bins. The agent must stop them and say where glass goes.
